name: Akirov Alfred
forbes_bio: Alfred Akirov is the founder and Chairman of Alrov Group, an Israeli real estate and hospitality company based in Tel Aviv.
Born in Iraq in January 1941, he immigrated to Israel with his family in 1952.
He began his career in construction at his father's business before venturing into textiles and fashion, and then shifting into real estate and investments.
He founded Alrov Group in 1978 and has since expanded the company into real estate, luxury hotels, and financial holdings both in Israel and abroad.

name: Kwee Liong Keng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Kwee Liong Keng and his three siblings control privately held Pontiac Land, which owns an array of luxury hotels and iconic office towers across Singapore.
Pontiac Land was founded by their Indonesian father Henry Kwee, a textile trader and real estate developer, who migrated to Singapore in 1958.
In New York, the brothers own a majority stake in a luxury tower designed by French architect Jean Nouvel, located beside the Museum of Modern Art.
In 2017, the brothers acquired the Cappella Hotel group from legendary luxury hotelier, Horst Schulze, for an undisclosed sum.
Pontiac Land has invested $400 million in a resort complex in the Maldives.

name: Gu Wei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Gu Wei chairs Shenzhen MTC, which makes consumer electronics products, including TVs, for brands such as Philips.
Shenzhen MTC trades on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange; Gu owns about half the company.
Gu holds a MBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

name: Kai-Uwe Hollweg
forbes_bio: Kai-Uwe Hollweg chairs the advisory board of Cordes & Graefe, the parent company of the GC Group, a wholesaler that covers a wide range of products for plumbing and HVAC systems.
Founded in 1921 as a pipe and tube trading company, Cordes & Graefe formed the GC Group in 1975 through a series of acquisitions.
Today the company is one of the largest wholesalers in the industry with $15.5 billion in sales (2022).

name: Kenzo Tsujimoto
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Kenzo Tsujimoto is the chairman and CEO of Osaka gaming company Capcom, which he founded in 1983.
Capcom is known for popular video games such as Resident Evil, Monster Hunter and Street Fighter.
His eldest son, Haruhiro Tsujimoto, is president and COO of Capcom while his youngest son, Ryozo Tsujimoto, oversees Monster Hunter.
Tsujimoto also owns the 3,800-acre Kenzo Estate in California's Napa Valley, of which 125 acres have been developed into vineyards.
forbes_facts: His wife Natsuko, who is COO of the winery, has set up five Kenzo Estate restaurants in Japan and an upscale restaurant in downtown Napa.
The Kenzo Estate site used to be the training ground for the U.S. equestrian team.

name: Martha MacMillan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Martha MacMillan is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, the world's biggest agriculture business.
Her great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.
The Cargill-MacMillan family collects an estimated 18% of net profits as dividends every year.

name: John Kusuma
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun Global (2022-2024)
forbes_bio: John Kusuma draws his wealth from a majority stake in Bank Aladin Syariah, previously Bank Net Syariah.
He acquired shares in the bank in 2019 and increased his holding in 2020.
The bank got listed in February 2021. Shares have soared since on expectations of the bank providing digital banking services.
Kusuma belongs to the third generation of the family behind cigarette-maker Nojorono Tobacco International.
forbes_facts: Bank Aladin Syariah's president is Dyota Marsudi, the son of Indonesia's foreign affairs minister, Retno Marsudi.
Founded in 1932 in Central Java, Nojorono Tobacco International is the country's fifth-largest cigarette maker, selling  an estimated10 billion sticks annually.

name: Melih Abdulhayoglu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2018-2019); Hurun Global (2020)
forbes_bio: Melih Abdulhayoglu's Comodo, which he founded in 1998 in the U.K., produces digital security products, notably SSL certificates for websites.
He moved the company to New Jersey in 2004 and in 2017, sold 50% to private equity firm Francisco Partners for an undisclosed sum.
Another Abdulhayoglu venture, eZLO, produces smart home automation technology that is compatible with Amazon Alexa.
He's also developing a client-server communication protocol for sharing access to files, printers, serial ports and other resources on a network.
These and other ventures are gathered within MAVeCap (Melih Abdulhayoglu Venture Capital), founded in 2018.
forbes_facts: He earned his first money in 1989 by winning a patent prize of 5,000 British Pounds offered by the British government.
His invention was a keyboard that could perform translations into multiple languages with one stroke.

name: Tong Jinquan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2010-2022); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2003-2026)
forbes_bio: Tong Jinquan chairs Summit Group, a privately-held real estate developer based in Shanghai.
An elementary school dropout, Tong built an empire that includes projects in Shenyang and Anshan.

name: Sun Huaiqing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Sun Huaqing chairs Guangdong Marubi Biotechnology, a supplier of cosmetics and skin care products.
Sun worked for an electric machinery factory in Chongqing more than 20 years ago.
He founded the "Marubi" brand in Guangzhou in 2000.
Marubi investors include L Capital, an affiliate of LVMH.
